title: For a good triple there is a finite presentation closed subscheme of the divisor on which the derived twist has locally free cohomology of the expected ranks
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: Letting X, D, I, M be as in Situation labelled situation-complex-and-divisor with (X, D, M) a good triple, the lemma produces a closed immersion i : T -> D of finite presentation such that T scheme theoretically contains D cap W for the maximal open W where the cohomology sheaves of M are locally free, the cohomology sheaves of Li^*L eta_I M are locally free, and the ranks of H^i(M)_x and H^i(Li^*L eta_I M)_t agree for t in T with image x in W (statement lines 13809-13829). On an affine chart (U, A, f, M^bullet) where all the ideals I_i(M^bullet, f) are principal, the proof defines T cap U inside D cap U by the ideal J(M^bullet, f) = sum_i J_i(M^bullet, f) of A/fA studied in More on Algebra, Lemmas labelled more-algebra-lemma-eta-vanishing-beta-plus-pre and more-algebra-lemma-eta-vanishing-beta-plus, the second of which also identifies the morphism T cap U -> D cap U with the ring map A/fA -> C (proof lines 13831-13842). Since the triple is good, such charts cover X and the first of the two lemmas shows that the construction glues, giving a closed subscheme T of D cut out by the ideals J(M^bullet, f) on good charts, and then properties (1) and (2) follow from the second lemma (proof lines 13844-13849; the author writes 'Details omitted' here and adds an observation that since eta_f M^bullet is a complex of locally free modules the restriction Li^*L eta_I M over T cap U is represented by eta_f M^bullet otimes_A C, after which property (3) follows from Cohomology, Lemma labelled cohomology-lemma-eta-cohomology-locally-free at proof lines 13851-13857). Gluing the local ideal construction and matching ranks through the locally free representative of the twist is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
